title: Wagertech (Kobi/Waleed internal, before client sync) - Transcript

items.topic: Go-live blocked on Deal CMS integration
items.statement: Kobi says go-live is blocked by the Deal CMS-Salesforce integration, although the system was designed to process sign-ups without a deal ID if market information is present.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: where we're scope creeping ourselves. we're blocked on going live because of this whole deal CMS Salesforce integration because that requires sending information about the deals either from Salesforce to the CMS which is then needed when they need to send those signup clicks back to Salesforce. we've designed the system to work independently regardless. so even if they don't send the deal ID, for example, as long as we have the market information and stuff, we can still process those signups and get as far as the signup creation and everything. But I feel like we're stuck. We have all this stuff that's almost ready, but they still keep wanting to make changes and finessing it, which is fine.
items.note: Internal Jumpr assessment; not a client statement.

items.topic: No API endpoint info or design sign-off
items.statement: Jumpr shared integration documentation; Jo left feedback but has not confirmed the design, and the client has not given API endpoint information, so integration development cannot start.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: that was last week. Yeah, we shared with them a whole bunch of documentation. Jo went through and left some feedback but nothing material like nothing I can work with yet she hasn't said we're good with that design and they haven't given us any API endpoint information or… / Kobi Kunasekaran: anything for us to start any development on our end for it. So yeah maybe today we go through and figure out what the next steps are and what we need to finalize those timelines.
items.note: Internal Jumpr assessment; not a client statement. 'Jo' may be Joyce [ASR?].

What do they need to do? what their plans are with this new rep assessment assignment I guess right and then whether or not we're going to go live with what we have manually I'm right that was last week's right / Kobi Kunasekaran: that was last week. Yeah, we shared with them a whole bunch of documentation. Jo went through and left some feedback but nothing material like nothing I can work with yet she hasn't said we're good with that design and they haven't given us any API endpoint information or…

items.topic: SLC processing works without deal ID
items.statement: Kobi says SLC click processing was updated to work even if the CMS sends only market, country and vertical instead of a deal ID, with lookups still done; this item is done.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the biggest one was the SLC click processing where we had only set it up so that the player information is all fine but for the deal the initial one assumed that a deal ID was going to be sent from their CMS which is true now that we're doing the integration but we've also updated that to still work even if all they send is the market country vertical like the breakdown of the deal and we're still able to do the lookups. So that one is done.
items.note: Internal Jumpr assessment; not a client statement.

items.topic: Fraud process still needs flows
items.statement: Kobi says everything from Jumpr's side is pretty much done except the fraud process, which needs a couple more flows; updating the status when fraud is dismissed is a quick piece that can be done between today and tomorrow.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah I think everything except maybe the fraud process needs a couple more flows. I think everything else is pretty much done from our end. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, it's almost like a preuat testing of that API layer. So, if we can do that this week, I think that's a pretty good win. And then that means that'll help us make sure everything else is in place. all of the other logic to process the signup is already good to go. the fraud flagging there there's that one piece where if they dismiss the fraud, we need to update the status. So that's a quick one like we can do that between today and tomorrow and…
items.note: Internal Jumpr assessment; not a client statement.

items.statement: UAT depends on the client doing real-world data tests with the sign-up click links on one of their agency websites, which Emily said they are working toward this week; Kobi calls this a pre-UAT test of the API layer.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: if we decide to go into UAT in a couple of days, we can because we can fit in the fraud process and there's nothing else that we need to do. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yes. Yeah, I'm just going through the board just to confirm that that's the last one. Oops. Yeah, I think that that's it. So, for us to go into UAT, I think we're still waiting for them to do real world data tests with the signup click links which they were supposed to do this week. that's what Emily said they're working towards having that ready for this week to hook it up to one of their agency websites so we can see the signups come through and see if it passes. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, it's almost like a preuat testing of that API layer. So, if we can do that this week, I think that's a pretty good win. And then that means that'll help us make sure everything else is in place. all of the other logic to process the signup is already good to go. the fraud flagging there there's that one piece where if they dismiss the fraud, we need to update the status. So that's a quick one like we can do that between today and tomorrow and…
items.note: Internal Jumpr assessment; not a client statement. Client commitment is as reported by Kobi, not heard from client in this meeting.

items.topic: Go live with manual deal rep assignments
items.statement: Kobi says Jumpr can go live if the client accepts creating deal rep assignments and deal configurations manually in Salesforce for now; Waleed says this was raised last week and it is the client's decision.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we can go live with that but that assumes that they are going to be creating those deal rep assignments and deal configurations in Salesforce with enough information that we can do the mapping when the signups come in. / Waleed Alasadi: we said that last week, so it's up to them to decide. I just wanted to know what their position is. So, … / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I think we can go live if … / Kobi Kunasekaran: if they're good with the manual creationable deal assignments in Salesforce for now. we should be good to go.
items.note: Client position not known in this meeting; client decision pending.

items.topic: Reps do not see full deals
items.statement: Waleed recalls last week's decision that reps will not see deals in full; Kobi confirms a simplified rep view, with extra information under 'more info', and that the client does not want reps to see the same information.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Last week we decided that reps are not going to see the deals entirely. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, there's two views that we need to look at, we've been working towards a simplified view for the reps where they didn't need all the info and then the information that she's looking for under more info for the reps. So that's how it's set up. I think they just want a line that's expected. and we're on the same page because they don't want reps to see the same information. true.
items.note: Earlier client-meeting decision as recalled internally.

items.statement: Kobi suggests making 'more info' the main deal view and bringing key information into the deal rep view, which depends on what key information must be added to rep assignments.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So if that's the case then we make the more info as the main thing and then we bring any key information into the deal rep view which I guess it goes back to what are those key information that we need to add into the rep assignments and then we can move that Okay.

items.topic: Small loose ends and ongoing feedback churn

items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: There's still loose ends Kobe like to tell you the truth even showing the Asana board there's a lot of up nexts they're small they're all small but to me they're loose ends still like that are open and… / Kobi Kunasekaran: Some of these I'm batting based on the new feedback that we keep getting. So that's why it feels like it's never ending because this more that just keeps coming. U so again happy to keep working on it but we need a end in sight. we need to put a foot down and move forward and then iterate once we have actual people in there. Otherwise, we're going to keep going back and forth. Yeah.
